subject: Acme POC: Success criteria & eval methodology - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme POC: Success criteria & eval methodology - next steps

Hi Priya / Sam -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary goal: improve customer support deflection by automating accurate triage and reply suggestions for ~20k monthly conversations.
- Key constraint: PII redaction required; no long-term retention of raw transcripts.
- Success metric target: 25% reduction in human handle rate OR average per-ticket reply time improvement of 30% (we should pick one primary).

Proposed success criteria (attached spreadsheet):
- Quantitative: Precision@K on suggested replies, reply acceptance rate, end-to-end SLA (latency).
- Qualitative: label-level accuracy on intent classification, and manual review pass rate >= 85% on sampled responses.

Evaluation approach (high-level)
1) Offline evals (week 1-2): Redwood runs an offline benchmark on a sample dataset you provide (anonymized). We score candidate models using the attached rubric (proposed_eval_rubric.docx) - metrics: semantic similarity, BLEU-ish, human-grade flags.
2) Online shadow (week 3-5): Shadow deployment where suggestions are generated live but not surfaced to customers; click/accept data collected to measure real-world acceptance and latency.
3) Ramp & validation (week 6-8): Controlled rollout (10% -> 50%) with monitoring and rollback gates.

Ownership (suggested)
- Redwood: infra + model hosting, eval harness, monitoring dashboards (Dylan).
- Acme: data export & anonymization, business acceptance (Priya), eng lead for integration (Bob).
- Joint: weekly check-ins and final sign-off on success criteria.

Open questions / needs from Acme
- Final owner for data export and estimated availability 
- Confirmation on which single success metric we use as the pass/fail gate
- Any compliance artifacts we need to pull ahead of the kickoff (SOC2, DPA)

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.xlsx, proposed_eval_rubric.docx

Next steps
- Can you confirm owners and the preferred primary success metric by Wednesday?
- If yes, I'll send a calendar invite for kickoff (we're proposing Thu next week).

Thanks -

Subject: Re: Acme POC: Success criteria & eval methodology - next steps

Thanks Priya - great, reply acceptance rate as the primary gate. Quick answers and a proposed concrete eval plan: 

Minimum dataset for offline eval
- ~2k representative conversations (anonymized). If you can provide stratified samples across 3 priority channels (email, chat, in-app), even better.

Proposed offline eval (week 1-2)
- Dataset: 2k de-identified conversations + ~500 gold labels for a manual grading pass.
- Metrics:
  * Reply acceptance rate (simulated using A/B labels from historical suggestion data)
  * Semantic Similarity (sentence embedding cosine)
  * Top-1 precision / NDCG for suggested replies
  * Manual grade pass rate (human reviewers, blind)
- Rubric: grade each generated suggestion as Accept / Needs Edit / Reject. Score pass if Accept >= 50% and Accept+Needs Edit >= 85% for the prioritized intent set. (See attached eval_rubric_v2.xlsx for templates.)

Online shadow plan (week 3-5)
- Run in shadow for 2 weeks at full traffic but not surfaced to users. Capture click/accept signals, latency, and model staleness metrics.
- Gates to move from shadow -> 10% surfacing: reply acceptance rate in shadow within 10% of offline predicted acceptance and average latency < 600ms (95th pctl).

Ownership (confirmed)
- Redwood (Dylan): infra + eval harness + dashboards.
- Redwood (Neha): manual eval coordination and rubric enforcement.
- Acme (Bob): data export, de-identification script, integration for shadowing.

Compliance note
- We can run the offline eval on a de-identified sample - token redaction is fine. We'll need the script you use for de-id so we can verify no PII is present before running.

Next steps (proposal)
1) Bob to share sample schema and anonymization script by EOD Wed (Aug 31).
2) Acme to confirm dataset availability for a Sep 6 offline eval kickoff.
3) Marissa to send calendar invite for Sep 1 kickoff to align stakeholders.

Attachments: eval_rubric_v2.xlsx

--Dylan
